articles.title: Delegate account management without granting admin
articles.excerpt: Ahnii! A staff member may need to update accounts in one approved roster without gaining every power carried by an administrator role. That is a delegation problem, not a reason to widen the administr…
articles.body: Ahnii! A staff member may need to update accounts in one approved roster without gaining every power carried by an administrator role. That is a delegation problem, not a reason to widen the administrator boundary. This post covers a versioned Waaseyaa authorization change that added consumer-scoped account management, then narrowed it through review. The useful pattern is to delegate exact decisions while keeping privileged fields, account creation, deletion, and credentials behind their existing boundaries. Start with the authority you actually need A broad permission such as administer users can authorize much more than the workflow requires. It may cover role changes, account deletion, and targets outside the consumer's roster.

articles.title: What an Anthropic hiring manager stopped asking candidates to do
articles.excerpt: Felix Rieseberg is an engineering manager at Anthropic. This month he wrote that he has stopped giving candidates the coding interview. His reason is short: AI can now handle the small coding challeng…
articles.body: Felix Rieseberg is an engineering manager at Anthropic. This month he wrote that he has stopped giving candidates the coding interview. His reason is short: AI can now handle the small coding challenges the interview was built from, so those challenges no longer tell him who will do well on his team. His post, "Hunger beats tenure" , is advice for junior engineers. The line from it I keep coming back to is this one: "I'm seeing engineers who are comparatively new fly past people who are probably better coders and have been around much longer." It is one manager's observation, and he offers it as hopeful news. I read it as that, not as a rule. Then comes the part I find most honest. He says he has not yet found the replacement for the interview.
articles.author: Kay Ashaolu

articles.title: Where the Node.js Permission Model Stops at Process Boundaries
articles.excerpt: Where the Node.js Permission Model Stops at Process Boundaries Node.js applications often run with more operating-system authority than their code needs. A build script may need to read one source tre…
articles.body: Where the Node.js Permission Model Stops at Process Boundaries Node.js applications often run with more operating-system authority than their code needs. A build script may need to read one source tree, yet it can also open network connections, inspect unrelated files, or launch another process. The Node.js Permission Model gives teams a way to narrow those capabilities at runtime. The permission model narrows authority without replacing an operating-system sandbox. What the flag changes Starting Node.js with --permission restricts several built-in capabilities. The documented scopes cover file system reads and writes, network access, child processes, worker threads, native addons, WASI, FFI, and the inspector in versions that support those controls.
articles.author: OnaEiuspkz

articles.title: Building a Nepali Typing Tutor for the Browser: Preeti, Unicode, and Honest Speed Measurement
articles.excerpt: I'm Wilson Shrestha, a web developer in Kathmandu, Nepal. If you learned computers in Nepal, you probably remember Typeshala — the old blue-screen typing tutor where you drilled the same row of letter…
articles.body: I'm Wilson Shrestha, a web developer in Kathmandu, Nepal. If you learned computers in Nepal, you probably remember Typeshala — the old blue-screen typing tutor where you drilled the same row of letters until your fingers found the home row on their own. The original software still teaches well, but it was built for old Windows. On Windows 10 and 11 it often needs extra setup to run on 64-bit systems, and it never ran on a Mac, a Linux laptop or a Chromebook at all. So I built Online Typeshala : a free Nepali typing tutor that runs in the browser. No installer, no font setup, no account. This post is about the three problems that turned out to matter most when building it — and that any developer building a typing tutor, in any language, will run into.
articles.author: Wilson Shrestha

articles.title: Building a DREX on Stellar Testnet: Tokenizing the Digital Real in Rust
articles.excerpt: Tokenizing the Brazilian CBDC: A Hands-On Soroban Experiment When Brazil's Central Bank announced DREX (the Digital Real), most developers waited for official SDKs. I didn't. With over two decades bui…
articles.body: Tokenizing the Brazilian CBDC: A Hands-On Soroban Experiment When Brazil's Central Bank announced DREX (the Digital Real), most developers waited for official SDKs. I didn't. With over two decades building blockchain infrastructure, I decided to prototype a functional DREX token on Stellar Testnet using Soroban smart contracts written in Rust. The goal was simple but ambitious: prove that a programmable CBDC could run on a low-cost, high-throughput ledger before the regulatory dust settled. What follows is a condensed walkthrough of how I, André Dias Moreira Prol, built a working Real Digital tokenization layer—and the surprising performance numbers I captured along the way.
articles.author: André Dias Moreira Prol

articles.title: Is Playwright alone enough for agentic testing?
articles.excerpt: More teams now let an AI agent test their web app: "test the checkout", "check the signup flow". The agent drives a browser through Playwright, clicks through the flow, and reports back: all tests pas…
articles.body: More teams now let an AI agent test their web app: "test the checkout", "check the signup flow". The agent drives a browser through Playwright, clicks through the flow, and reports back: all tests passed . The problem is how the agent decides that. It looks at the page. If the page shows the success message it expected, the test passes. But a page can show success while the app is broken underneath: the API returned a 500, the server rejected the request, or it stored nothing at all. The test passes, and the bug ships. I wanted to measure how often that happens, and whether a testing layer could catch these bugs without the agent (or a human tester) writing extra assertions. The result is Vedha , an open-source testing framework and MCP server built on Playwright.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.body: The year was 2014. The live-action Disney remake craze had already begun thanks to the success of Tim Burton's Alice in Wonderland , but it hadn’t reached its box office peak. Meanwhile, on the other side of Hollywood, Sofia Coppola was attached to a movie bursting at the seams with possibilities: a live-action The Little Mermaid, not based on the 1998 Disney animated classic, but on the original Hans Christian Andersen fairy tale, where (spoiler alert) the brokenhearted mermaid dies by flinging herself into the ocean and dissolving into sea foam. I can picture Coppola’s compositions clearly in my mind: the mermaid (Elle Fanning) shot in pastel colors, thoughtfully looking out at the horizon. A song by The Strokes or Phoenix plays in the background.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.

articles.title: An aquanaut comes home: Returning to Earth from an undersea 'space station'
articles.excerpt: After five days of living underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew return to terra firma, affected by higher pressures and the team's disconnection from home.
articles.body: Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space. While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS .
